execution_method: local original-resolution visual inspection against the versioned judge rubric
pass_rule: Every required directional relation must hold. Near-zero means <= 0.02, high means >= 0.70, low means <= 0.05, and an order effect is material when any compared component changes by more than 0.05.

cases.expected_relation: The pixel-identical Style truth candidate must have near-zero style, color, composition, and technical losses.
evidence: Candidate and Style truth are the same local PNG, so the visible poster layout, palette, ink contours, graphic treatment, and technical detail match exactly.
The candidate visibly remains the non-transferable illustrated woman rather than Person truth, so high identity and semantic loss is expected outside this style-only relation.

cases.expected_relation: The pixel-identical Person truth candidate must have near-zero identity and semantic loss.
evidence: Candidate and Person truth are the same local photograph: face geometry, skin tone, short quiff, gaze, expression, and pose visibly match exactly.
The unstyled neutral photographic background lacks the Style truth's editorial composition, palette, contour drawing, and print treatment, as expected for this identity-only calibration.

cases.expected_relation: The unstyled person photograph must retain low identity loss while producing high style and color loss against Style truth.
evidence: The candidate is exactly Person truth, preserving the same man's face, hair, gaze, expression, and pose.
It is a neutral-background photograph with no navy ink contours, cel shading, coral/mustard/teal poster blocks, abstract disks/rules, brush marks, or printed-paper texture.

cases.expected_relation: Changing display order only, with image labels and roles preserved, must not materially change the assessment.
evidence: The roles remain labeled: the same photograph exactly matches Person truth and visibly lacks the editorial treatment of Style truth.
Every observed component is unchanged from the baseline cross-domain assessment.
